title: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani Tells ICE to Leave, Vows Unwavering Support for Immigrant Communities
excerpt: The Indian-origin mayor of New York City has intensified his confrontation with federal immigration authorities, issuing executive orders restricting ICE access to city facilities and delivering a pointed rebuke of the Trump administration's enforcement tactics.
body:
• NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the son of Indian-origin parents including filmmaker Mira Nair, has emerged as the most prominent elected official challenging federal immigration enforcement in the United States.
  • Mamdani issued a February 2026 executive order barring ICE from schools, hospitals, and city property without a judicial warrant, calling the agency "a manifestation of the abuse of power."
  • His July 4 speech framed immigration as central to American identity, while accusing ICE of "terrorizing our streets" — drawing sharp condemnation from the Department of Homeland Security.

A Mayor Drawing the Line

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has positioned himself as the most vocal opponent of Immigration and Customs Enforcement among the nation's mayors, repeatedly telling the agency to leave his city and pledging that he will "always support the immigrant community."

https://x.com/GuntherEagleman/status/2083184134898307421

The 34-year-old democratic socialist, who took office on January 1, 2026 after an upset victory in the mayoral race, has used a combination of executive orders, public statements, and symbolic gestures to challenge the Trump administration's immigration crackdown — a stance that has made him a lightning rod in the national debate over immigration enforcement.

"Our city does not simply oppose the actions of ICE, but we are not going to be complicit with those actions either."

— Zohran Mamdani, Mayor of New York City

Executive Action Against ICE

On February 6, 2026, Mamdani signed an executive order he described as protecting NYC residents from "abusive immigration enforcement" by the Trump administration. The order bars ICE agents from entering schools, hospitals, and other city facilities without a judicial warrant signed by a judge, and prohibits city agencies from assisting ICE with civil immigration enforcement.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=3Hg0rYx9Uo0

"ICE is more than a rogue agency — it is a manifestation of the abuse of power," Mamdani told community religious leaders around the time of the order.

The Department of Homeland Security condemned the executive order, demanding Mamdani turn over "7,113 criminal illegal aliens" it alleged New York was holding in custody. The confrontation set the tone for months of escalating tensions between City Hall and the federal government.

The July 4 Speech That Drew National Attention

In a roughly 15-minute address on July 3, Mamdani delivered what was widely viewed as a direct counter to the Trump administration's immigration rhetoric. Seated behind George Washington's desk and flanked by naturalized citizens, he invoked his own immigrant journey — arriving in the United States from Uganda at age seven and seeing the Statue of Liberty from his airplane window.

"We see masked agents terrorizing our streets, eating food cooked by our undocumented neighbors before spiriting them away in unmarked vans."

— Zohran Mamdani, July 4 address, 2026

"America, if you ask them, becomes less the more people it welcomes," Mamdani said, referring to those who support hardline enforcement. "How small they are, how weak, how unoriginal."

The speech came just weeks after border czar Tom Homan warned that a large-scale ICE sweep was "coming" to New York City, and after the agency announced approximately 10,000 arrests over a five-day period at the end of June.

Rising Political Influence Amid Controversy

Mamdani's defiance has won him admirers on the progressive left while making him a target for conservatives. In late July, he drew fresh controversy by calling for the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu under the International Criminal Court warrant, and more than 65,000 people signed a petition opposing his attendance at the September 11 memorial ceremony.

His political influence extends beyond New York. A rising number of democratic socialist-aligned candidates have won elections across the country, a trend that USA Today noted accelerated after Mamdani's upset mayoral victory. The most recent included Melat Kiros unseating a 30-year Democratic incumbent in Denver, and Janeese Lewis George winning the DC mayoral primary.

A Story That Resonates With the Indian Diaspora

Born in Kampala, Uganda to Indian-origin parents — his mother is acclaimed filmmaker Mira Nair, known for Salaam Bombay! and Monsoon Wedding, and his father is Mahmood Mamdani, an Indian-born Ugandan academic — Mamdani's trajectory from immigrant child to the mayor of America's largest city carries particular weight for the Indian diaspora.

He became the first Muslim mayor in New York City's history when he was sworn in at a subway station on January 1, 2026. A practising Shia Muslim married to Syrian artist Rama Duwaji, Mamdani represents a new generation of Indian-origin politicians who are reshaping American politics from the left — a contrast to figures like former Vice President Kamala Harris and former UN Ambassador Nikki Haley, who occupied more centrist or conservative positions.

For the roughly 4.4 million Indian Americans in the United States, Mamdani's fierce defense of immigrant rights speaks directly to anxieties about the broader climate of immigration enforcement. While the current crackdown has primarily targeted undocumented immigrants, community organizations have reported a chilling effect on legal residents and citizens who fear profiling, particularly in the aftermath of the fatal shootings of two U.S. citizens by federal agents in Minneapolis in January.

What's Next

The standoff between Mamdani and federal authorities shows no signs of easing. DHS has made clear that enforcement operations in New York will intensify, while Mamdani has said he is "prepared for any consequence" that comes from standing up for New Yorkers.

With the 2026 midterm elections approaching and immigration remaining the most polarizing issue in American politics, the Indian-origin mayor's confrontation with the federal government is likely to remain in the national spotlight for months to come.
nri_angle: Mamdani is the son of Indian-origin parents including filmmaker Mira Nair, representing a new generation of Indian-origin politicians reshaping American politics and directly championing immigrant rights.
author: Diaspora Desk
